label: cor:spectral-decomposition-qvalue
title: Spectral decomposition of the $\mathcal{Q}_q$-value over the torus knot basis of $\Sigma_4$
html:
This is a direct consequence of the cohomological embedding (completeness of the torus knot basis on \Sigma_g) applied to the beta decay transfer matrix.

Let \Sigma_g be a genus-g surface and \mathcal{E}_g = \{\tau(r,s) : \tfrac{(r-1)(s-1)}{2} \leq g\} the set of torus knot labels embeddable on \Sigma_g. For \beta^- decay \mathcal{N}_{Z,N} \to \mathcal{N}_{Z+1,N-1}, the Q-value admits the spectral decomposition:

  Q
  = 
  \underbrace{
    \Bigl|\log_q\frac{P_{\mathrm{dau}}(q)}{P_{\mathrm{par}}(q)}\Bigr|
    \cdot \hbar_q \cdot \frac{m_e}{3}
  }_{\displaystyle\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}}}
   \times 
  \underbrace{
    \prod_{\tau(r,s) \in \mathcal{E}_g}
    F\!\bigl(\tau(r,s), N\bigr)
  }_{\displaystyle\text{knot operator product}},

where:

(i) P(q) = \prod_{j=0}^{A-2} \hat{V}_j(q) is the Skein polynomial from the inductive chain construction (transfer matrix). Each chain \hat{V}_j = z \cdot M_j[0][0] + M_j[1][0] (with Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) \approx 0.612688037 at q_0) is pre-reduced via the 2\!\times\!2 matrix recurrence. This requires zero Hecke steps. It ensures \mathcal{N}_{Z,N} is in Gröbner--Shirshov normal form at every inductive stage.

At z = q^3/(q^2+1), each transfer-matrix factor \hat{V}_j and hence P(q) has coefficients in \mathbb{Q}(q) with no half-integer powers of q; the numerical evaluations of \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}} are tabulated in the interpretation.

(ii) \log_q(x) = \ln x / \ln q is the q-natural logarithm. It counts exceptional divisor levels along the color tube fiber of \Sigma_g. The constant \hbar_q = (q - 1)/q is the quantum Planck constant. This is the action per divisor step. The factor m_e/3 is the mass per crossing of the electron word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (electron), which has 3 letters. (The backup trefoil electron \mathcal{K}_{\tau(2,3)} also has 3 crossings, so the factor is the same in both readings.) The product \hbar_q \cdot m_e / 3 replaces the intermediate notation \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{int}} \cdot \mu_0. These cancel algebraically.

(iii) F(\tau(r,s), N) is the knot operator of \tau(r,s) acting on the converting neutron's shell:

  F(\tau(r,s), N)
  = 
  \begin{cases}
    1
    & \tau(r,s) \notin \mathcal{E}_g
     \text{ (null: zero action on \(\Sigma_g\))} \\[4pt]
    1
    & \text{shell unchanged by decay (cancels in ratio)} \\[4pt]
    \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
      \tau(r,s) \cdot T_{\beta\text{-decay}}(q)
    \bigr)
    & \text{active shell, partially filled} \\[4pt]
    \dfrac{\bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
      e_{(1^3)} \cdot \tau(r,s) \cdot
      T_{\beta\text{-decay}}(q) \cdot e_{(1^3)}
    \bigr)\bigr|}{\bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(T_{\beta\text{-decay}}(q)\bigr)\bigr|}
    & \text{active shell, fully filled (Pauli)}
  \end{cases}

with T_{\beta\text{-decay}}(q) = \sigma_0 \sigma_1^{-1} \in H_3(q) the beta decay operator (beta decay), and e_{(1^3)} the alternating Young symmetrizer of H_3(q) (glossary).

At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the fourth case is degenerate: the Ocneanu weight of every partition with three rows vanishes, so \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(e_{(1^3)} \cdot x \cdot e_{(1^3)}\bigr) = 0 for every x \in H_3(q), and the fully filled branch returns F = 0 and hence Q = 0 on every magic-number shell; no non-vanishing replacement projection has yet been derived. The corollary is therefore asserted only for decays whose converting shell is not fully filled. The fully filled (magic-number) case is excluded from its scope, because on that case the formula returns Q = 0, which is not a Q-value.

(iv) The product over \mathcal{E}_g collapses to a single term. Only the converting neutron's shell knot \tau(k^*) is active. All other shells cancel between parent and daughter. Non-embeddable knots contribute F = 1.

(v) On the scope fixed in (iii), the decomposition is exact. The embeddable torus knots form a complete basis for the representation ring of H_n(q) restricted to \Sigma_g, by the self-duality \tau(r,s) \leftrightarrow \tau(s,r) and the Rosso–Jones completeness of torus knot invariants (cohomological embedding). No higher-order corrections exist; the tower terminates definitively at degree \lfloor 2g/(g-1) \rfloor.
